title: fleet discovery & node inventory playbook
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and playbook for service discovery + node/cluster inventory model used by the inference control plane and routing layer. Focus is on consistent node metadata (labels), GPU capability taxonomy, health signals to drive routing & lifecycle actions, and how inventories replicate across regions. This is a working playbook — iteration expected.

Problems we need to solve
- Reliable, searchable inventory of nodes (region/zone/pool) with stable IDs and machine/GPU capabilities.
- Fast discovery for router decisions (latency-sensitive fallback, capacity-aware routing).
- Meaningful health scoring (not just binary ready/failed) for graceful degradation and autoscaling triggers.
- Cross-region eventual-consistent view for routing policies (affinity, failover) without central bottleneck.

High-level design
- Inventory service (control plane component) owns canonical records for nodes and GPUs. It exposes a small query API used by routers and autoscalers.
- Each region runs a localized inventory replica (read-optimized), synced from the canonical regional control plane via event stream (Kafka/pubsub). Global control-plane aggregates metadata for admin UI and global routing decisions.
- Node agent pushes heartbeat + health metrics to regional ingest endpoint (TLS + mTLS). Agent also reports NVML-derived GPU metrics.
- Inventory model is tag/label first. Labels are primary keys for routing policies (avoid coupling to instance names).

Label / taxonomy proposal (canonical keys)
- node.id: stable UUID across reboots (prefer instance metadata + salt)
- node.region: e.g., us-west-2
- node.zone: e.g., us-west-2a
- node.pool: e.g., gpu-serving, infra, build
- node.role: serving | staging | infra | batch
- hw.cpu_count: integer (vCPUs)
- hw.memory_gb: integer
- gpu.count: integer
- gpu.brand: nvidia | amd
- gpu.family: a100 | h100 | rtx6000 | mi250
- gpu.arch: ampere | hopper | rdna2
- gpu.memory_gb: integer
- gpu.compute_score: short string (e.g., "fp16:fast,int8:ok,tensor:yes")
- gpu.features: comma-separated (tensor-cores, mig, mig-isolated, ecc)
- runtime.driver_version: semver-like string
- runtime.cudnn_version: string (if applicable)
- node.features: batching=true|false, kvcache=true|false, direct_io=true|false
- availability: on_demand | reserved | spot | preemptible

Notes on GPU fields:
- Keep both normalized fields (gpu.family, gpu.memory_gb) and a freeform compute_score for quick capability matching. The router prefers explicit fields but can fall back to compute_score heuristics when exact match missing.

Health signals (collected by node agent)
- last_heartbeat (RFC3339 timestamp)
- agent_version
- node.uptime_seconds
- cpu.load_1m, cpu.load_5m
- mem.free_mb, mem.total_mb
- disk.io_wait_ms (per-disk aggregated)
- gpus[*].util_pct (per GPU)
- gpus[*].memory_used_mb, gpus[*].memory_total_mb
- gpus[*].temperature_c
- gpus[*].power_draw_w
- gpus[*].pci_errors (correctable/uncorrectable)
- nvml.ecc_errors_total (rolling 24h)
- driver.error_count (recent kernel oops etc)
- pods.evicted_last_1h (k8s cases)
- network.egress_mbps, network.ingress_mbps

Health scoring model (example)
- Compute a 0-100 health score per node. Start at 100 then subtract penalties:
  - missing heartbeat > 30s: set score=0 (unavailable)
  - gpu.util_avg_1m > 95% AND queue_length > threshold: -20 (saturated)
  - gpu.temperature_c > 85C: -30
  - nvml.ecc_errors_total > 10 (24h): -40
  - mem.free_mb < 10%: -20
  - cpu.load_1m > cores*2: -15
- Map score bands: 80-100 healthy, 50-79 degraded (serve but prefer alternatives), 1-49 avoid (fallback only), 0 unreachable (drain/cordon).

Routing & policy integration
- Router accepts a policy expression referencing labels and health bands. Examples:
  - primary: region=us-west-2 && gpu.family in (h100,a100) && health>=80
  - fallback: region!=us-west-2 && health>=60 && availability!=spot
  - cost-aware: prefer availability=reserved and batchable=true for low-priority jobs
- Policies compiled to scoring functions; inventory query returns top-N candidates with health and capacity hints. Router picks one based on latency/cost/routing-weight.
- For streaming/short-latency requests: prefer local-region healthy nodes; if none, automatically fail to cheapest-compatible regional replica (policy param).

Multi-region replication model
- Each region writes its node events to a regional event topic. Global control plane subscribes and maintains an aggregated index (eventual consistency).
- Router uses local region cache for fast decisions and consults global index only for cross-region fallback logic to avoid extra RTT.
- Conflict resolution: node moves (reprovisioned in new region) should create new node.id; previous id gracefully transitions to drained status after TTL.

Operational playbook (what to do on signals)
- Health score <50: auto-cordon node (set schedulable=false), notify SRE, schedule drain if serving pool.
- Persistent ECC errors OR driver failures: automatic unenroll into "replacement" pool and create ticket JIRA-1198 (example).
- Sudden drop in gpu.count reported (hotplug/failure): mark node as degraded immediately and alert.
- Stale agent (no heartbeat 1m): place node into quarantined state and try to reach agent via SSH-run diagnostics.

API & query expectations
- Inventory API: /v1/nodes?labelSelector=...&min_health=60&region=us-west-2&limit=50 -> returns list of node ids + label map + health_score + capacity_hint (available_gpus, queue_depth_est).
- Lightweight index service used by router should be read-optimized (Redis + protobuf cache). Full records stored in canonical DB (CockroachDB/Postgres).
- Cache TTLs: health metrics TTL = 10s for router cache; node metadata TTL = 5m.

Deployment concerns & telemetry
- Agent efficiency: keep payloads small (snapshots of top signals) and use delta updates for high-frequency metrics.
- Backpressure: if ingest slow, sampling rate for gpus[*].util_pct can be dropped. Important signals (heartbeat, driver error) never sampled out.
- Telemetry: expose per-region counts: nodes_total, nodes_healthy(>=80), nodes_degraded, avg_health_score. Instruments drive routing fallback rate metric.

Migration & compatibility notes
- Support legacy labels for older clusters with mapping layer (e.g., "gpu_type" -> "gpu.family").
- Model versioning: inventory schema carries a schema_version field; router resolves older versions via a compatibility layer.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent MIG-like multi-instance GPUs cleanly in label model while keeping query simple? (option: gpu.instance_counts + instance_type enum).
- Exact health scoring weights — propose A/B test in staging with traffic mirroring.
- Throttle policy for routing to prevent cascades when an entire region is degraded.
- Define SLOs for inventory propagation (regional local cache consistency windows).

Quick checklist for implementation
- [ ] Inventory schema v1 spec (canonical keys + types)
- [ ] Node agent: minimal heartbeat + NVML metrics + delta encoding
- [ ] Regional ingest + event topic + stream consumer for canonical DB
- [ ] Local router cache with TTLs and API shim
- [ ] Health scoring service + ruleset UI in Console
- [ ] Alerts & automated remediation playbooks

References / notes
- Slack thread: #platform-node-inventory (pinned: design sketches)
- Related tickets: JIRA-1198 (node ECC handling), JIRA-1282 (router fallback policy), PR #418 (inventory service prototype)

Notes to self:
- Keep label keys very small and stable. Avoid ad-hoc label explosion.
- Prefer querying by capability (e.g., "supports:fp16") rather than brand names in higher-level policy definitions.

End of playbook (working draft)
